stories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, CFO Colette Kress steps in
stories.dek: The co-founder quits effective immediately amid reported affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and an Nvidia executive, as the board names its first chair.
stories.body:
Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia. "Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately," the company said in a press release announcing a CEO transition. Chief financial officer Colette Kress becomes interim CEO and keeps her CFO duties while the board searches for a permanent successor. Nvidia says it "will consider internal and external candidates."

The board also appointed Harvey Jones as its first-ever chairperson. "I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years," Kress said in the release. The company thanked Huang for his "immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry."

The exit follows reports that Huang had an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a firm tied to a $2 billion chip smuggling case in Singapore. Tom's Hardware reports she is suspected of helping sanctioned Chinese companies obtain hundreds of thousands of banned H100 and H200 chips, and that $7.5 billion worth of banned chips reportedly reached China. Citing Bloomberg, it says she has now surfaced in Beijing. The FBI is examining the relationship, and the Chinese embassy in Washington calls the claims "groundless smears and slanders." A second report alleges an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's VP of health care.

Pressure from Washington continues. Congress has threatened a subpoena if Huang does not attend a closed-door briefing with the heads of the House committees on China, Foreign Affairs and Intelligence. PC Gamer reports that meeting is set for November 18, the same day Kress has called a company-wide meeting and one day after Nvidia's next earnings call.

Kress has been CFO since 2013 and previously held senior finance roles at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments. PC Gamer reads her appointment as a move to steady investors, comparing it to Intel's 2018 handover to interim CEO Bob Swan after Brian Krzanich's ouster. In an email to staff, reported by CNN's Hadas Gold, Kress called this "an extraordinarily difficult period."

The succession race is already political. According to PC Gamer, President Donald Trump has backed Tim Cook, while the House China Select Committee wants a leader who "makes national security its top priority." What happens to Huang's legal exposure, and to Nvidia's, remains unclear.
key_points: Huang quits as CEO, president and board member, effective immediately
CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO; internal and external candidates considered
Harvey Jones becomes Nvidia's first board chairperson
FBI and Congress probing Huang's ties to suspected spy Alice Huang
stories.why_it_matters: Nvidia's GeForce, CUDA and AI roadmaps now sit with a finance chief and a board under political pressure, so the next permanent CEO will shape what Nvidia prioritizes for developers and gamers.

cover.caption: Jensen Huang's run at Nvidia, per interim CEO Colette Kress

sources.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Orchestrator

stories.headline: Google ships Gemini 4 Hydrogen to everyone, replacing 3.8 Flash
stories.dek: The fast, cheaper model skips the staged rollout given to Carbon and Argon and arrives with Orchestrator, which switches models mid-task.
stories.body:
Google has released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the replacement for Gemini 3.8 Flash, the fast and economical model most people in Google's ecosystem use. Ars Technica notes that the rollout breaks from recent practice. Google's Argon and Carbon releases started with cybersecurity researchers, and general availability was then limited to subscribers on the most expensive AI plan. Hydrogen is available immediately and has replaced 3.8 Flash across Google's products.

Google says Hydrogen finishes tasks 2.5 times faster than 3.8 Flash at its default high thinking level. The company also says it cuts fabricated claims by more than 5x and more than triples Flash's Terminal-Bench 4.1 score, from 18.2 percent to 57 percent. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Google reports Hydrogen scores 51 at high and 54 at a new xhigh setting, against 50 for Argon, one of its frontier models. The four thinking levels are low, medium, high and xhigh.

Pricing is flat across the full 1 million-token context window: $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. The model is rolling out globally in AI Studio, the Gemini API, Android Studio, Gemini for business, the Gemini app and Google Search. In Google Antigravity, Google's coding environment, it is limited to paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

Alongside Hydrogen, Google launched Orchestrator in Antigravity. Instead of a static router that picks one model from the first prompt, Orchestrator hands work back and forth within a single session. Carbon can plan in a read-only phase, Hydrogen writes edits and runs tests, and Carbon takes over again if Hydrogen hits trouble. Google says Orchestrator reached near-Carbon success rates on Terminal-Bench while using 24 percent less quota on average and finishing 19 percent faster. Google's main announcement cites version 4.0 of the benchmark for that result, while the Antigravity post cites 4.1.

Orchestrator access is narrower than Hydrogen's. Ultra subscribers get Orchestrator (Carbon) and Orchestrator (Argon). Paid Pro subscribers get only the Argon version. Enterprises get both through Gemini for business. All performance figures come from Google's own testing.
key_points: Gemini 4 Hydrogen replaces 3.8 Flash across Google products, available immediately
Priced at $1.50 input and $7.50 output per million tokens
Google claims 2.5x speed and 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.1, up from 18.2%
Orchestrator switches between Carbon and Hydrogen within one Antigravity session
stories.why_it_matters: Developers on Flash get a faster, cheaper default model with a 1 million-token context at flat pricing. Orchestrator tests whether mixing a frontier model and a fast model in one session can save quota without losing quality.

cover.caption: Hydrogen's claimed speedup over Gemini 3.8 Flash at default settings

sources.title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories

stories.headline: Hijacked GitHub accounts plant CI secret stealer in 1,806 repos
stories.dek: The wfx-loot campaign used 4,837 stolen accounts to probe 61,764 repositories for write access, then grabbed Actions secrets and cloud credentials.
stories.body:
An attacker used stolen credentials for 4,837 GitHub accounts to probe 61,764 repositories and run a CI secret stealer in at least 1,806 of them, according to Aikido Security. BleepingComputer, citing the researchers, puts confirmed theft at 1,835 targets. The campaign, dubbed wfx-loot, began November 10 with pull requests titled "docs: dependency audit notes" from a wfx-docs branch.

The 1,500-line script grabs Actions secrets, GITHUB_TOKEN, OIDC tokens and AWS, Azure and GCP credentials, plus keys for OpenAI, Anthropic and other tools. It can plant backdoors that survive rotation. The attacker then reverted changes and deleted run logs. SafeDep counted 8,093 repositories with malicious commits.

A Packagist package and Go modules were also affected. Owners should check for missing run numbers and rotate all secrets.
key_points: Aikido says 4,837 hijacked accounts probed 61,764 repos and ran the stealer in at least 1,806.
The script steals CI secrets and cloud credentials and can create backdoors that survive rotation.
Packagist's digitalelvis/neuronai-studio 3.14.3 is malicious; affected repo owners should rotate all secrets.

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: Hackers Exploit N-central Flaws to Infect 21 Servers, Including 19 Running Hotfix 2

stories.headline: N-central zero-day hits 21 servers hours after exploit goes public
stories.dek: Attackers used the 4EverAble2Shell chain to install Monero miners, and 19 of the compromised servers were already running N-able's Hotfix 2.
stories.body:
Attackers began exploiting a new N-able N-central zero-day called 4EverAble2Shell within hours of researcher Sean Bales publishing a proof-of-concept on November 12. Security firm Huntback says at least 21 production servers were compromised to run XMRig Monero miners, 19 of them on version 2026.4.1.26, the Hotfix 2 release from November 10. Infected servers sit in countries including the US, Canada, the UK, Germany, France, South Africa and Sweden.

The chain pairs Apache Axis flaw CVE-2026-90436 (CVSS 9.8) with an N-central privilege escalation to gain unauthenticated root access, according to Previdian. It requires the Legacy API to be enabled. Bales also released Agent2Shell, which he says yields SYSTEM access on Windows.

N-able has disabled its Intune integration and urges customers to keep Legacy API off. "Treat a hit as a full compromise," Huntback said.
key_points: Huntback found 21 N-central servers mining Monero, 19 of them already patched with Hotfix 2.
Exploitation attempts started around 08:30 UTC on November 12, shortly after the PoC release.
N-able restricted features, disabled Intune integration and says Legacy API should stay disabled.

sources.title: New SignDrop Zero-Day Exploit Turns Windows CLFS Security Feature Into SYSTEM Access

sources.name: BleepingComputer
sources.title: New Windows SignDrop zero-day gives hackers SYSTEM privileges

stories.headline: SignDrop exploit turns Windows CLFS protection into SYSTEM access
stories.dek: A researcher's unpatched proof of concept abuses a CLFS log-authentication feature Microsoft added in October 2025, using Defender as the privileged trigger.
stories.body:
A researcher has published exploit code called SignDrop that claims to let a standard Windows user gain SYSTEM privileges through the Common Log File System driver. Microsoft has not confirmed the flaw, assigned a CVE or released a fix, The Hacker News reports. The code appeared on GitHub on Tuesday, the same day as November's security updates.

The exploit targets a log-authentication check Microsoft added in October 2025 to curb CLFS attacks. When a privileged process, here the Defender antimalware service, opens a prepared log, the driver creates a companion .cnpf file as SYSTEM. Symbolic links redirect it to a location the attacker can write to.

A tester at Korean firm 78researchlab confirmed it works but found it unreliable. Systems with the CLFS Authentication Mode registry value at 0 or 1 are in scope. Disabling the mitigation reopens older memory corruption flaws.
key_points: SignDrop abuses CLFS log authentication, added in October 2025, to create a user-writable file as SYSTEM.
Microsoft has issued no CVE or patch, and no attacks using the exploit have been reported.
Machines with CLFS Authentication Mode set to 0 or 1, the default on established installs, fall within the claimed scope.

sources.name: The Hacker News
sources.title: Node.js Fixes 16 Flaws, Including HTTP/2 Bugs That Crash Servers and Leak Other Connections' Data

stories.headline: Node.js patches 16 flaws, including HTTP/2 crash and data leak bugs
stories.dek: Unauthenticated clients could crash default HTTP/2 servers on 24.x and 26.x or pull other connections' data, and updating is the only fix.
stories.body:
Node.js has released fixes for 16 vulnerabilities, seven rated high, in versions 22.23.5, 24.22.3 and 26.13.1. The worst let unauthenticated clients crash servers or read memory belonging to other connections, The Hacker News reports.

The crash flaw, CVE-2026-123863, hits default HTTP/2 servers on 24.x and 26.x that reply before a request body fully arrives, which the project calls typical. A second HTTP/2 bug, CVE-2026-123866, can send clients pieces of server memory, including responses meant for others, on all three lines. A separate HTTPS flaw, CVE-2026-123864, can leak memory "including TLS private keys and other users' requests," the project says.

The advisory lists no workarounds and reports no attacks. End-of-life lines such as 20.x and 25.x get no fix. Chris Rohlf reported five of the flaws with Claude and Anthropic Research.
key_points: Fixed versions are 22.23.5, 24.22.3 and 26.13.1; end-of-life 20.x and 25.x stay vulnerable.
CVE-2026-123863 lets unauthenticated clients crash default HTTP/2 servers on 24.x and 26.x over TLS or cleartext.
The advisory lists no workaround and reports no known attacks.

sources.name: Google DeepMind
sources.title: Google DeepMind releases AlphaGenome 2 for predicting effects of DNA variants

stories.headline: DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 nearly doubles hits on likely causal variants
stories.dek: The DNA variant model trains on more than 100 million single-cell profiles across 68 tissues and recovers 30 percent of likely causal variants on TenK10K.
stories.body:
Google DeepMind has released AlphaGenome 2, a model that predicts the effects of DNA variants. The company says the new version recovers 30 percent of likely causal variants on TenK10K, up from 16 percent for the first AlphaGenome.

The gain comes with a much larger training set. AlphaGenome 2 is trained on more than 100 million single-cell profiles spanning 68 tissues. DeepMind frames the work as a step toward understanding how cells read DNA and, from that, how genetic variation contributes to disease.

DeepMind announced the model on November 11. The core research team includes Žiga Avsec and Pushmeet Kohli, and DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis is also credited among the contributors.
key_points: AlphaGenome 2 recovers 30 percent of likely causal variants on TenK10K, versus 16 percent for the first version, according to DeepMind.
The model is trained on more than 100 million single-cell profiles across 68 tissues.
Google DeepMind announced the release on November 11.
